sonnet.problem: Ahab and Elijah show up for the first time with no label saying who they are (for example 'Ahab, Israel's earlier king' and 'Elijah, the prophet'). Jehonadab son of Rechab is also named with no short label.
sonnet.rule: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

sonnet.problem: Baal is named in the quoted line and in the questions that follow, but no card says he is a false god. The baker needs that for the assembly and the killing to make sense.
sonnet.rule: When a place, nation, false god, title or role needs explaining for the moment to make sense, he says in a few words what it is, like "Kedar, a desert tribe" or "Tammuz, a false god."

sonnet.problem: The joke calls Jehu "Mr. Zeal for the LORD himself" right after Jehu says he will serve Baal a lot. That signals the speech is not sincere, which is the answer to the later true/false card 5 ("Jehu is truly planning to serve Baal"). It also ignores that the text says he is acting deceptively.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The story card says "Baal's gone from Israel. But there are also the golden calves..." The "But" signals that Jehu did not turn away from them. That gives away the answer to card 6 and rules out the wrong answer "He tears them all down too."
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The card tells Jehu's death and burial ("rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria") and also carries a joke ("the Jehu highlight reel"). That joke also plays on the way Scripture refers to the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel, and it comments on how he tells the passage ("which I'm calling").
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.
